feedback_source: Curated from prior judge and Python feedback, including weak-weather and residual interpretations in the latest Luna run.
analyst: Machine-readable recommended_plan.estimated_bill and savings must be decimal amounts without currency symbols, for example 85.94. Currency symbols belong only in copied display metrics. Copy supplied metric values including signs and units. For mathematical_justification, copy metric_id keys only from summary.metrics with the exact corresponding values; do not put peer_comparison_status there, because it has its own output field. In explanation include {{bill_total}}, {{daily_change}}, {{feb_days}}, and {{march_days}}. Include {{bill_change}} in either the headline or the explanation. Associate each billing period with its month explicitly: February had {{feb_days}} days and March had {{march_days}} days. Avoid respectively. Keep synthesis focused on the measured change, a qualified possible explanation, a practical action and any supported plan savings. Use ordinary language in headlines and actions; technical detail belongs in mathematical_justification. When the weather fit is weak or the period is outside the training range, say the weather evidence is insufficient to determine its role; never claim weather did not cause or explain the increase. The weather_residual is the percentage difference between actual use and the weather-model estimate, relative to that estimate; it is not the percentage of total use that is unexplained. For a weak or extrapolated fit, retain weather_residual in mathematical_justification when required, but do not interpret or attribute that percentage in prose. Describe the measured demand pattern and qualify any possible cause.
communications: Prior semantic review found customer captions too technical. Use ordinary phrases such as steady electricity use or electricity use throughout the day. Explain a baseline increase as your home starting to use more electricity even during quieter hours. Keep technical terms and power-unit measurements out of customer captions. Write one short, qualified possible reason and one useful check; avoid presenting a possible device or cause as proven. For example: Something may be running longer; check equipment timers and overnight schedules. The template supplies the numbers, charts and plan savings, so focus on understandable meaning. Preserve every supported uncertainty.
